slideDifferences.nativeText:
Cultural Shock

You realize about the differences in countries when you finally go and live somewhere else. That happened to me when I went to study in Taiwan. It is called the sleepless city since stores and business are supposed to stay open all night. Don’t get me wrong, I think it is acceptable to have some business and stores open, but all of them? Well, that is not the custom for us to have in my country. Normally, stores open in the morning and they closed at nights , so people are expected to go during that time; however, some folks are used to go 10 minutes before closing and I do believe you are not supposed to do that.

Have you had a similar experience?

slideDifferences.publishedText: I wasn’t prepared for the culture shock of being an international student For any student, moving away from home can be daunting. But I didn’t expect student life in Scotland to be all that different from my home of the Netherlands. After all, we get the same news and TV shows online. However, when I moved from Amsterdam to study at the University of Stirling, I began to realise that a few small things were catching me off balance. I was suffering a minor cultural shock. In my first year, I quickly found out my English was not as good as I had assumed. Most of my flatmates were born and raised in Scotland, and I constantly found myself having to ask people to repeat themselves. Their Scottish accents didn’t help and I was mispronouncing names and places all the time. I also got confused about small cultural things. Much to my flatmates’ amusement, it took me two Christmases to figure out that mince pies are not actually filled with minced beef. The language barrier meant that public transport was tricky at first. I found the lack of information about bus prices and how and where to get tickets really surprising. It turned a simple 15-minute journey into a daunting task. texts: In my country, you are supposed to say your first name when introducing yourself

What are you supposed to do when…?

Am I expected do something special?
People are not expected to hug others in Asia.
It is not acceptable for women to wear miniskirts in Dubai.
It is the custom to double kiss in some European countries.

To Consider
These expressions are not the only ones we can use. 
There are different ways on how we can ask about customs and traditions. 
Simple present is also useful to talk about this matter.
There are many ways in which we can state our ideas regarding customs. Check the following chart.
